cards.title: Introduction to Testing in ASP.NET Core
cards.content:
Testing is a crucial part of building robust ASP.NET Core applications. We primarily focus on three types of tests:

  • Unit Tests: Test individual components (like services or business logic) in isolation.
  • Integration Tests: Test multiple components working together, such as controllers interacting with databases.
  • End-to-End (E2E) Tests: Test the entire application flow from the user interface down to the database.

content.question: Which type of test typically verifies business logic in a single class without involving the database or network?

cards.title: Unit Testing with xUnit and Moq
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core projects typically use xUnit as the testing framework. To isolate the class under test, mocking frameworks like Moq are used to simulate dependencies.

[Fact]
public void GetProduct_ReturnsCorrectProduct()
{
    // Arrange
    var mockRepo = new Mock<IProductRepository>();
    mockRepo.Setup(repo => repo.GetById(1)).Returns(new Product { Id = 1, Name = "Laptop" });
    var service = new ProductService(mockRepo.Object);

    // Act
    var result = service.GetProduct(1);

    // Assert
    Assert.Equal("Laptop", result.Name);
}

content.text: In xUnit, to verify that two values are equal, we use the Assert._____(expected, actual) method.

cards.title: Integration Testing using WebApplicationFactory
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core provides the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing package, which includes WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint>. This allows you to spin up an in-memory test server to send real HTTP requests to your API.

public class ProductsApiTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    private readonly HttpClient _client;

    public ProductsApiTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
    {
        _client = factory.CreateClient();
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetEndpoints_ReturnsSuccessAndCorrectContentType()
    {
        var response = await _client.GetAsync("/api/products");
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
        Assert.Equal("application/json; charset=utf-8", response.Content.Headers.ContentType.ToString());
    }
}

An HTTP request is sent to the target API endpoint.

cards.title: Testing Best Practices Summary
cards.content:
Key takeaways for testing in ASP.NET Core:

  • Write fast unit tests for business logic using xUnit and Moq.
  • Use WebApplicationFactory for reliable integration tests against HTTP endpoints.
  • Always design your services with Dependency Injection (DI) to make them easily testable.
  • Keep tests isolated, repeatable, and independent of external state where possible.
